devices.label: SURFboard SB8200 DOCSIS 3.1 cable modem
devices.description: DOCSIS 3.1 cable modem with 32x8 bonded SC-QAM DOCSIS 3.0 channels plus 2x2 OFDM/OFDMA DOCSIS 3.1 channels, bridged to two 10/100/1000Base-T LAN ports off a single F-connector coax input.
devices.notes: Vendor spec table: two 1 GB Ethernet ports, 32 DS x 8 US DOCSIS 3.0 + 2x2 OFDM(A); datasheet rates the RF side at 10 Gbps DS / 2 Gbps US over 108-1218 MHz. Both LAN ports are bridged, so the pair shares one client-side MAC domain (no NAT, no routing).

devices.label: SURFboard S33 DOCSIS 3.1 cable modem
devices.description: DOCSIS 3.1 cable modem with 32x8 SC-QAM plus 2x2 OFDM/OFDMA channels, giving one 2.5GBASE-T port and one 1GBASE-T port from a single coax drop.
devices.notes: Vendor page lists 'One 2.5 Gigabit Ethernet Port and One 1 Gigabit Ethernet Port', 2 OFDM x 2 OFDMA DOCSIS 3.1 channels and 32x8 DOCSIS 3.0 bonding. The asymmetrical port pair is the point: a 2.5G client can exceed 1 Gbps while the second port stays gigabit.

devices.label: CM1000 Ultra-High Speed DOCSIS 3.1 cable modem
devices.description: DOCSIS 3.1 cable modem with 32 downstream / 8 upstream DOCSIS 3.0 SC-QAM channels plus 2 OFDM downstream and 2 OFDMA upstream channels, bridged to a single gigabit Ethernet port.
devices.notes: Datasheet 'Physical Specifications': One (1) LAN Gigabit Ethernet port, One (1) WAN coaxial cable connection. NETGEAR's own footnote caps throughput at the 1G port even though DOCSIS 3.1 allows 10 Gbps DS.

devices.label: Nighthawk CM2000 2.5Gbps DOCSIS 3.1 cable modem
devices.description: Nighthawk DOCSIS 3.1 cable modem with 32x8 SC-QAM plus 2 OFDM / 2 OFDMA channels and a single 2.5GBASE-T LAN port.
devices.notes: Datasheet 'Standards': One (1) LAN 2.5Gbps Gigabit Ethernet port, One (1) WAN coaxial cable connection; 32 DS / 8 US SC-QAM + 2 OFDM + 2 OFDMA. Exactly one LAN port - no aggregation trick available.

devices.label: Nighthawk CM3000 mid/high-split DOCSIS 3.1 cable modem
devices.description: Mid/high-split DOCSIS 3.1 cable modem with 32 SC-QAM plus 2 OFDM downstream and 8 SC-QAM plus 2 OFDMA upstream channels, exposing one 2.5GBASE-T port and two aggregateable 1GBASE-T ports.
devices.notes: User manual Table 5 'Technical specifications': Local one 2.5 Gbps RJ-45 port, Aggregate two 1 Gigabit RJ-45 ports, Internet coax DOCSIS 3.1; channels 2 OFDM + 32 SC-QAM DS, 2 OFDMA + 8 SC-QAM US. The two 1G ports bond for ~2 Gbps when the router supports LAG.

devices.label: MB8600 DOCSIS 3.1 cable modem, 4x GigE
devices.description: DOCSIS 3.1 cable modem with 32x8 DOCSIS 3.0 fallback plus DOCSIS 3.1 OFDM/OFDMA, and four gigabit LAN ports that can be link-aggregated for up to 3.8 Gbps of delivered throughput.
devices.notes: Datasheet: 'Four (4) 10/100/1000 Gigabit Ethernet LAN ports, with Auto-MDI/MDIX' and an F-type female 75 ohm service interface. Four ports exist because the modem is limited to 1 Gbps per port; 2-port bonding gives ~2 Gbps, 4-port ~3.8 Gbps.

devices.label: MB8611 DOCSIS 3.1 cable modem, 2.5G
devices.description: DOCSIS 3.1 cable modem with 32x8 DOCSIS 3.0 and DOCSIS 3.1 OFDM/OFDMA support, offering a single 2.5GBASE-T LAN port rated to 2,500 Mbps downstream.
devices.notes: Motorola support spec page: 'One 2.5 Gigabit Ethernet (GigE) LAN port (supports 10/100/1000/2500 Mbps)', downlink up to 2,500 Mbps / uplink up to 800 Mbps, SNMP v1/v2/v3 management.

devices.label: MARLIN L CGA4236 DOCSIS 3.1 cable gateway
devices.description: DOCSIS 3.1 / EuroDOCSIS 3.1 cable gateway with 32x8 bonded channels plus 2x2 OFDM(A), four GE LAN ports (one 2.5GBASE-T plus three gigabit), dual-band Wi-Fi 6, two FXS voice ports and a USB 3.1 port.
devices.notes: Spec sheet: '4 GE LAN ports (1 2.5 Gigabit Ethernet and 3 GE LAN ports optional)', 2x2 OFDM(A) D3.1 / 32x8 D3.0, 2 FXS, 1 USB 3.1 Gen 1, Wi-Fi 6 3x3 @2.4 GHz + 4x4 @5 GHz. Coax rated 5 Gbps DS (3.6 Gbps with 2 OFDM, up to 5 Gbps with 32 SC-QAM added). Unlike the pure modems above this one routes, NATs and serves DHCP, so it terminates the LAN.

devices.label: E6000 Converged Edge Router (Gen 2: RSM-2 + DCAM-2 + UCAM-2)
devices.description: Integrated CCAP / CMTS chassis modelled with the Gen 2 module set: one RSM-2 plus RPIC-2Q giving 3x 100G QSFP28 and 10x 10G SFP+ network-side uplinks, one DCAM-2 with 16 downstream RF ports and one UCAM-2 with 24 upstream RF ports across 12 connector groups.
devices.notes: Counted: DCAM-2 = '16 physical ports per slot' (MCX, requires DPIC-2); UCAM-2 = '24 physical ports organized into 12 connector groups', 288 SC-QAMs (12 per port) + 2x 96 MHz OFDMA per port; RSM-2 = 2x 100G QSFP28 + 2x 10G SFP+ on the front panel, RPIC-2Q adds 1x 100G QSFP28 + 8x 10G SFP+ (3x 100G / 10x 10G total per RSM pair), plus 100/1000BASE-T mgmt RJ-45 and an RJ-45 console. One downstream and one upstream module are modelled; the chassis holds many more CAM slots, so per-service-group port maths has to be scaled by the module count an operator fits.

devices.label: cBR-8 Converged Broadband Router (CCAP)
devices.description: 13 RU, 10-slot CCAP chassis (8 subscriber-side line-card slots, 2 supervisor slots) modelled with one CBR-LC-8D31-16U31 line card: 8 downstream and 16 upstream coax ports, plus a supervisor PIC carrying two 100G QSFP28 NSI uplinks and two RJ-45 GE management ports.
devices.notes: Datasheet Table 1: '13 RU and 10-slot chassis (8 subscriber side slots, 2 supervisor slots)', '64 service groups (56 SG with N+1) for ICCAP', '8DS ports X 16 US ports'; per line card 768 D3.0 QAMs plus 2 OFDM blocks per DS port and 96 US channels plus 2 OFDMA blocks per US port. Supervisor PIC = 'Two Integrated 1x100G NSI backhaul interfaces' + 'Two RJ45 GE network management ports'. One line card is modelled of 8 possible; a fully loaded chassis would be 64 DS / 128 US ports.

devices.label: C100G Converged Cable Access Platform (CCAP)
devices.description: 13 RU, 14-slot CCAP chassis (12 subscriber slots + 2 switch/management modules) modelled with one DS8x96 downstream module (8 F-type DS ports), one 16-port US upstream module and an SMM8x10G switch module providing eight 10G SFP+ uplinks.
devices.notes: Casa datasheet: '13 RU, 14 slot chassis (12 subscriber slots, 2 management modules)'; 'RF I/O Downstream Module (RFD): Number of ports 8 per module, Connector F-type, 75 ohm'; 'RF I/O Upstream Module (RFU): 16 or 32 ports per module - 16 port F-type, 32 port MCX'; SMM8x10G = eight 10GbE; mgmt = RS232 RJ45 + 10/100BASE-T. Capacity: 1,024 DS channels per DS card, 6,144 DS channels in a fully loaded chassis, up to 255 service groups with DAA.

devices.label: CableOS Reef Dense Remote PHY Shelf (1 line card modelled)
devices.description: 2 RU passive Remote PHY shelf for Harmonic's CableOS virtualised CMTS, housing 9 hot-swap line cards each carrying two independent Pebble RPDs of 1DS x 2US; modelled here with a single line card, so 2 downstream and 4 upstream coax ports.
devices.notes: Counted: '9 linecards per chassis, each with 2 RPDs' => 18 RPDs / 18 service groups; 'each with two independent Remote PHY devices of 1DSx2US ports' => 2 DS + 4 US per line card (18 DS / 36 US fully loaded). RPD spec: up to 158 SC-QAMs or 6x 192 MHz OFDM per RPD, 5-204 MHz US, 1218 MHz DS. A full shelf is modelled as one line card because only one card's worth of RF ports is needed to represent a service group pair; the RPD uplinks are Ethernet tunnels to the CableOS Core (software vCMTS on a 1-RU x86 server) and the datasheet publishes no connector count for them, so none are modelled.

devices.label: Opti Max OM6000 1.2 GHz 4x4 HFC segmentable node
devices.description: 1.2 GHz 4x4 segmentable HFC optical node that terminates the fibre node in a DOCSIS plant: four forward RF segment outputs and four return RF segment inputs, 10 application module slots in the lid for optics, EDFA, PON extension or a Remote PHY device.
devices.notes: Counted: 4x4 switchable segmentation => 4 forward + 4 return RF segments; 'provisions for ten optics modules in the lid and four RF modules in the base', 10 application module slots + 2 SG4 auxiliary slots, 6 housing ports total, optical connector SC/APC, 54/85/102/258-1218 MHz DS with upstream to 204 MHz. The optical side is not modelled as a port because the lid modules are ordered separately (analog Rx/Tx, digital return SFP, or an RPD); this node is the RF boundary in the simulator, not an IP host.

devices.label: CODA60 DOCSIS 4.0 mid/high/ultra-high tri-split cable modem
devices.description: DOCSIS 4.0 cable modem with switchable mid (5-85 MHz), high (5-204 MHz) and ultra-high (5-396 MHz) upstream splits against a 1794 MHz downstream, supporting 5 configurable 192 MHz OFDM channels and 32 SC-QAM downstream, presented as a single 10GBASE-T LAN port.
devices.notes: DOCSIS 4.0 reference point. Datasheet: '1x RF F-Type 75 ohm Female Connector, 1x RJ-45 10GBASE-T Ethernet Port'; D4.0 support for 5 OFDM channels up to 192 MHz and 7 OFDMA channels up to 96 MHz, 32 SC-QAM DS / 8 SC-QAM US bonded; tri-split 108-1794 / 258-1794 / 492-1794 MHz DS. Deploys in DOCSIS 3.1 mode first and upgrades in place.

devices.label: Vigor166 G.fast & VDSL2 35b supervectoring modem
devices.description: G.fast (106/212 MHz, up to 1 Gbps) modem/router that falls back to VDSL2 profile 35b supervectoring and ADSL2+, with one RJ-11 DSL port and two gigabit Ethernet LAN ports.
devices.notes: Vendor page: '1x RJ-11 for G.fast/VDSL2 35b/ADSL2+' and '2x GbE RJ-45' LAN. G.fast gives 1 Gbps on short loops (hence 1G on the DSL side here); VDSL2 35b is capped at 300 Mbps and ADSL2+ at 24 Mbps. Bridgeable to a separate router, so it appears as both modem and (optionally) router.

devices.label: Vigor167 VDSL2 35b supervectoring / ADSL2+ modem
devices.description: VDSL2 profile 35b supervectoring and ADSL2+ modem/router with a single RJ-11 DSL port, two gigabit Ethernet LAN ports and an SPI firewall.
devices.notes: Vendor spec table: 1x VDSL2 35b/ADSL2+ RJ-11 WAN, 2x GbE RJ-45 LAN, RJ-45 console, SNMP v2/v2c/v3, TR-069. VDSL2 35b tops out at 300 Mbps down, but the port class is the copper xDSL class - 100M is the conservative line rate; 35b vectoring is what lets it exceed it on short loops.

devices.label: DM200 Broadband High-Speed VDSL/ADSL modem
devices.description: VDSL/VDSL2 and ADSL/ADSL2+ bridge modem with auto-detection for universal DSL, one RJ-11 DSL port and exactly one 10/100 Ethernet LAN port.
devices.notes: Datasheet 'Standards': 'One (1) LAN Ethernet RJ-45 port' and 'One (1) VDSL/ADSL RJ-11 port'. The datasheet omits the LAN rate; the user manual's LED table settles it - 'green for 100 Mbps and amber for 10 Mbps' - so it is a 10/100 port, not gigabit. Single LAN port means only one device or one router can hang off it.

devices.label: TD-W9970 300Mbps Wireless N USB VDSL2 modem router
devices.description: VDSL2/ADSL2+ modem router with a 2.4 GHz 802.11n access point, one RJ-11 DSL port, four 10/100 Ethernet LAN ports and a USB 2.0 port for storage or printer sharing.
devices.notes: Datasheet 'Interface': 4x 10/100Mbps RJ45 ports, 1 RJ11 port, 1 USB 2.0 port. VDSL2 per ITU-T G.993.2 with ADSL2+ fallback; 2x 5dBi fixed antennas, 802.11b/g/n only (2.4 GHz). Note the LAN side is Fast Ethernet, so this box cannot pass more than ~94 Mbps even on a fast VDSL2 line.

devices.label: SmartAX MA5600T DSLAM/OLT (4x 64-port VDSL2 boards)
devices.description: 10U copper/fibre access shelf used as a large-capacity DSLAM: 23 board slots (2 SCU control, 16 service, 2 GIU uplink), modelled here with four 64-port VDSL2 over POTS vectoring boards and four 10GE GIU uplinks.
devices.notes: Counted: MA5600T-ETSI/IEC subrack 'supports 23 board slots', 16 service slots, 2 SCU slots, 2 GIU slots; 'Maximum uplink port (GIU): 4*GE, 4*10GE'; 3.2 Tbit/s backplane. VDSL2 boards available: H805VDSF 24-port, H80BCVME 48-port VDSL2+POTS combo, H80DVCPM 64-port VDSL2 over POTS with vectoring (chosen here). Shelf maximum is 768 VDSL2 or 1024 ADSL2+ ports in a fully loaded subrack - this spec models 4 of the 16 service slots (256 VDSL2 lines) to keep the port list usable in a lab topology; scale board count for a full subrack.
